author: Codex independent assessor

source_artifacts.claim: Current level 16 definition: bubble attack, STOP/STEADY/RESCUE effects, ferry/bridge, lethal regions, collectibles, exits, and two boss target pads.
Current bridge, pad, motor, power, stabilization, slime, and exit helper definitions used by level 16.
Position 2 introduces an Isp-held door, a two-cell latched powered lift, and a Gem bubble as earlier concepts.
Position 4 introduces Isp's STOP effect on a motorized ferry and a latched RESCUE gate.
Position 3 introduces Pac's held STEADY effect on an unstable bridge and Isp's latched RESCUE route opening.
Position 17 introduces a Pac-held bubble lane that lifts Isp toward a rescue pad.
Position 24 uses a heavy delivery with Pac STEADY, Isp RESCUE, and an unstable bridge before this room.
Held pads release when vacated, latched pads remain active, and their effects stop, power, stabilize, or open barriers.
Both owner-specific boss target pads must be occupied; level 16 has no timed charge requirement.
Hazard overlap and falling below the world are lethal; each hero must reach their own exit and the boss must be defeated.
Bubble hits float Isp and make Pac sticky temporarily; the special descending Pac top contact is handled separately as a bounce.
A newly active listed interruption pad clears the attack's projectiles and returns the attacker to cooldown.
A descending Pac can bounce from the top of a bubble; other bubble contact applies its temporary effect.

prior_knowledge.concept: Basic two-character movement/jump controls, hold-to-open doors, latched route rescue, and Gem bubble avoidance are introduced before this room.

evidence.claim: The position 1 room defines an Isp hold pad, Pac-only latched RESCUE gates, movement key instructions in its hint, and Gem bubble/boomerang attacks.

prior_knowledge.concept: Isp can hold STOP to stop a motorized ferry and open the other hero's gate; a second hero can cross and activate RESCUE.

evidence.claim: Position 4 explicitly assigns Isp STOP to a motorized ferry and Pac's route includes crossing to latched RESCUE.

prior_knowledge.concept: Pac can hold STEADY to stabilize a bridge while Isp crosses; Isp can then latch RESCUE to preserve the bridge and open a route for Pac.

evidence.claim: Position 3 defines the Pac-held STEADY bridge and Isp-latched RESCUE stabilization and door effects.

prior_knowledge.concept: A player can use an earlier liver bubble for lift; this room's bubble attack is not required by the sampled no-effect completion route.

evidence.claim: Position 17 uses Pac's BUBBLES hold pad to float Isp toward RESCUE, preceding the current bubble interaction.
The current-source no-effects wait-and-walk trace completes both exits; bubble use is an available assist rather than a mandatory mechanic in that sampled route.

prior_knowledge.concept: Pac STEADY and Isp RESCUE with an unstable bridge and route gates were practiced in the immediately preceding room, then recombined with a moving ferry and simultaneous boss targets.

evidence.claim: Position 24 assigns Pac STEADY and Isp RESCUE to preserve an unstable bridge and open route barriers.

prior_knowledge.concept: Defeating Gem by occupying separate Isp and Pac target pads at once is a new mechanic at this roster position.

evidence.claim: Level 16 defines owner-specific TARGET pads as Gem's boss target pads; earlier source cues cited above introduce the component pad and gate mechanics, not this boss condition.

mechanics.fact: The mandatory route is a three-pad dependency: Isp's held STOP stops the press_ferry and opens Pac's island gate; Pac's held STEADY powers the ferry, stabilizes factory_bridge, and opens Isp's bridge gate; Isp's latched RESCUE restores ferry/bridge support and opens Pac's shutdown gate. Releasing a hold pad removes its effects; RESCUE persists after Isp leaves.

evidence.claim: Current spawn positions, ferry/bridge, pad ownership/effects, and three gate definitions.
Hold pads are occupancy-based, latch pads persist, and pad effects control doors and platform state.
Independent source-aware route summary identifies the same Isp STOP, Pac STEADY, Isp RESCUE handoffs and separate targets.

mechanics.fact: The lair_bubble launches toward the center after its windup. A hit makes Isp FLOAT or Pac temporarily STICKY; Pac can instead bounce from a descending top contact. STEADY or RESCUE interrupts the attack. Bubble use is avoidable in a current-source both-exit trace.

evidence.claim: The attack's aim, windup, cooldown, and interrupting pads are authored here.
Bubble effects for Isp and Pac are temporary movement interference, not a lethal hit.
The specified active pads interrupt the attack and clear its projectiles.
A descending Pac can top-bounce rather than receive the usual bubble effect.
A no-effects ordinary-input replay completed both exits, so the bubble is not required by that sampled completion.

mechanics.fact: Both owner-specific TARGET pads must be occupied together to defeat Gem; after that, each hero must overlap their own exit. The source has two slime regions below the crossing route and Gem's lethal core. The authored bridge collapses if unsupported for 0.8 seconds and resets after 2 seconds.

evidence.claim: Current ferry, bridge, pads, slime/core hazards, owner-specific target pads, and exit locations.
An unsupported bridge collapses after 0.8 seconds and respawns after 2 seconds.
Both target pads need the named owners; this boss has no authored charge duration, so simultaneous occupancy defeats it without an extra timer.
Hazard contact and falling below the world kill; completion requires the two owner-matched exits and a defeated boss.

legal_routes.name: STOP ferry, STEADY bridge, RESCUE, dual target, exits (source-derived; current native clear)

steps.goal: Open Pac's route to the control island while keeping the ferry stopped.
steps.action: Isp occupies STOP. Pac leaves the start island, crosses the adjacent stopped ferry, and reaches STEADY.
steps.expected_feedback: STOP holds the ferry motor off and opens Pac's island gate. The source hint names this sequence; the 36-room current-native replay completes, but its output does not record a human response or each transition.

evidence.claim: The authored hint and Isp-owned STOP effects define the opening handoff.
A retained ordinary-input trace reaches current-native-clear under the current source hash; this confirms feasibility of one sampled input sequence, not human discovery.

steps.goal: Power the ferry and make the bridge safe for Isp's crossing.
steps.action: Pac remains on STEADY. Isp leaves STOP, boards the now powered ferry, crosses to the control island, and continues over factory_bridge.
steps.expected_feedback: STEADY powers press_ferry, stabilizes factory_bridge, and opens isp_bridge. The hold must remain active until RESCUE takes over those supports.

evidence.claim: Pac's held STEADY pad powers the ferry, stabilizes the bridge, and opens Isp's bridge gate.
Leaving a hold pad removes its effects unless another active pad supplies them.

steps.goal: Latch RESCUE on the shutdown island to preserve support and open Pac's last gate.
steps.action: Isp crosses the powered ferry/steady bridge and occupies RESCUE; Pac holds STEADY until the latch is active.
steps.expected_feedback: RESCUE stays active after Isp leaves, restores ferry motor/power and bridge stability, and opens Pac's shutdown gate. It also interrupts the bubble attack.

evidence.claim: Isp's RESCUE latch supplies the route support and Pac shutdown access.
The retained current-native clear ends with RESCUE latched and both target pads occupied.

steps.goal: Defeat Gem and reach both matching exits.
steps.action: Isp occupies blue_target while Pac occupies orange_target; after Gem is defeated, each moves to their own exit on the shutdown floor.
steps.expected_feedback: Both owner-specific pads must be occupied together for Gem to be defeated. Each character still needs their matching exit; one hero at the wrong exit does not satisfy both-exit completion.

evidence.claim: The boss target pads are Isp/Pac-specific and the exits are also owner-specific.
Boss defeat requires simultaneous target-pad occupancy by the named heroes.
Both heroes must overlap their own exit after the boss condition is met.
The current-source retained route ends complete with both matching exits overlapped.
The level's authored route hint, causal pad effects, hazards, target pads, and exits.
The replay contract says current LEVELS and current engine were used with recorded player inputs only; the level 16 result is listed as a current-native clear.
The current-native replay result records completion, no deaths, both exits, and current source binding for level 16.

steps.goal: Complete the same mandatory route without relying on a bubble effect or bounce.
steps.action: Use the pad-and-platform route, waiting or walking through the available safe approach rather than depending on the bubble for lift or a boost.
steps.expected_feedback: The current-source trace summary identifies a wait-and-walk completion requiring no bubble effects; it does not establish that every recovery state is safe.

evidence.claim: The current-source wait-and-walk ordinary-input trace completes with no effects and no deaths.
The current-source ordinary-input wait-and-walk result terminates complete; this is a bounded simulation, not a human trial.
The route arrays were replayed against current assembled LEVELS and step_game, with no actor or state injection.

isp: Hold STOP to stop the ferry and open Pac's first gate.
After Pac reaches STEADY, cross the ferry and bridge, then latch RESCUE to preserve support and open Pac's shutdown gate.
Occupy the Isp-only blue TARGET at the same time as Pac's orange TARGET, then reach the Isp exit.
pac: Cross the stopped ferry to the control island and hold STEADY to power the ferry, stabilize the bridge, and open Isp's crossing.
Keep STEADY active until Isp's RESCUE latch takes over; then reach the Pac-only orange TARGET with Isp on blue TARGET and use the Pac exit.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac releases STEADY before Isp has reached RESCUE.
common_mistakes.consequence: The ferry loses the STEADY power override, the bridge is no longer held stable, and Isp's route gate can close; a hero already crossing may have to return to the control island.
common_mistakes.recovery: A retained current-source ordinary-input variant releases STEADY early, returns Pac, and completes both exits without a death. This supports recovery for that tested release-and-return case, not every possible fall.

evidence.claim: The tested early-release trace recovers in the same run; the report explicitly limits that conclusion to sampled mistakes.
The current-source probe says Pac’s early-release-and-return trace completed with both exits.
STEADY hold effects are removed on release and RESCUE later supplies those same supports.

common_mistakes.mistake: Isp misses an early useful bubble-float opportunity while trying to cross.
common_mistakes.consequence: The player misses an available boost and must wait for a later opportunity; the bubble effect itself is temporary and not lethal.
common_mistakes.recovery: A retained current-source trace waits for a later boost and still completes; a separate wait-and-walk trace needs no bubble effect at all. This suggests low recovery burden for the sampled cases, not that every bubble contact is harmless in every position.

evidence.claim: The missed-boost route waits for another opportunity and completes both exits with no deaths.
The bubble gives Isp a 1.4-second FLOAT effect and is not defined as direct lethal damage.

common_mistakes.mistake: Both support effects are absent while a hero is crossing the ferry/bridge, or a hero misses the supporting platform entirely.
common_mistakes.consequence: The unsupported bridge collapses after 0.8 seconds and the slime/core region is lethal on contact; a fall could end the run and require restarting the room.
common_mistakes.recovery: No allowed current-input evidence tests a lethal fall or room restart for this mistake. Source defines bridge respawn, but that does not establish a hero's safe recovery from the slime below; recovery cost in this severe case remains unresolved.

evidence.claim: Ferry, bridge, and lethal slime/core placements lie on the route.
The bridge itself resets after collapsing, while its existence does not prove that a falling hero survives.
Slime/core overlap and falling below the world cause death.

optional_collectibles: factory_blue (Isp-owned) at x=780,y=420 on the bridge area and factory_orange (Pac-owned) at x=580,y=410 on the control island; both are optional and neither is part of the both-exit/boss condition. The replay summary does not report whether either was collected.

reasoning.rationale: The authored dependency is more than the one cue visible in the idle frame: STOP opens Pac's gate, STEADY powers the ferry while stabilizing the bridge and opening Isp's gate, RESCUE must take over those supports, and then two owner-specific targets must be occupied together to defeat Gem. That is several ordered causal dependencies. The hint makes the intended plan more direct than a sustained hidden-mechanic puzzle, so 3 is more fitting than 4.

evidence.claim: The hint and authored pad/boss definitions show the three-stage route plus simultaneous target condition.
A current-source route reached the boss-defeated both-exit completion state.

cooperation.rationale: The mandatory route repeats mutual support: Isp first enables Pac's crossing, Pac enables Isp's crossing, Isp's latch restores Pac's route, and both must occupy separate boss targets simultaneously before reaching their own exits. This meets the repeated mutual-dependency/coordination anchor.

evidence.claim: The pads alternate ownership and the boss condition requires both owners at once.
The boss target condition requires both Isp and Pac-specific target pads occupied together.
Current route and mistake probes assign separate tasks to both heroes through the finale.

execution.rationale: The route uses a moving ferry, a bridge that is unsafe without a held or latched stabilizing pad, and deliberate landings on three separated control/target pads. Those are noticeable movement and placement demands, but the sampled ordinary-input routes complete with no deaths and source provides stable support while the pads are held; there is no evidence for sustained precision at level 3 or 4.

evidence.claim: The mandatory traversal crosses a moving ferry and bridge and requires landing on support and target pads.
The current-source ordinary-input route completes with zero engine deaths.

timing.rationale: The press_ferry has a repeatable motion period and a seven-of-ten-second power cycle, so a pair may need to wait or board as it moves. Pac's STEADY and Isp's RESCUE provide a continuous power override during the key crossing, however, and no narrow or chained window is required by the authored route.

evidence.claim: The ferry has a repeatable motion/power cycle and is powered by STEADY/RESCUE.
An active power pad overrides the mover's ordinary power state while held or latched.

hazards.rationale: The ferry and bridge cross slime-covered gaps, and Gem's core is lethal on contact. A successful route can stay on the ferry/bridge and use the stabilizing pads, but an unsupported crossing or bad landing can be fatal. This is visible danger with a supported safe approach, not repeated unavoidable exposure.

evidence.claim: Slime lies below the ferry and bridge, with a lethal villain core in the crossing area.
Contact with an active hazard or falling below the world sets a terminal death state.
Four current-input paths, including an attack-avoidance route, complete without deaths; this is sampled feasibility, not proof of novice safety.

novelty.rationale: STOP ferry control was introduced earlier, Pac's bridge stabilization and RESCUE latch were taught earlier, and the immediately preceding delivery room combines STEADY with RESCUE. The new transfer is to a Gem fight where those familiar supports feed a simultaneous two-target boss condition; the bubble offers another familiar interaction rather than a required new mechanic.

evidence.claim: STOP/motorized ferry is introduced at position 4.
STEADY bridge support and a RESCUE latch are introduced at position 3.
The immediately preceding room recombines STEADY, RESCUE, unstable bridge, and gates.
This room's source adds the simultaneous owner-specific boss targets.

recovery_cost.rationale: Two tested mistakes recover in the same run: Pac returns after releasing STEADY early, and Isp waits for another bubble boost. The first repeats some crossing setup; the second is optional because a wait-and-walk trace succeeds without the bubble. A lethal unsupported fall remains a separate untested case, so the rating describes the evidenced common corrections and not every failure state.

evidence.claim: Early-release and missed-boost routes, plus a no-effect route, all complete in the same run without deaths.
STEADY/RESCUE support and lethal falling hazards distinguish recoverable pad mistakes from an unsupported fall.

solution_clarity.rationale: The screenshot labels STOP, STEADY, RESCUE, TARGET, and both exits, and the visible character instructions name relevant abilities. The exact dependency order and the need to defeat Gem via the two targets are not explained by the idle scene; the authored hint supplies that route, but it remained closed during the first pass and is not counted as a base cue.

evidence.claim: The canvas visibly labels the pads and exits while the status line does not explain the handoff or boss target condition.
The hint describes the route, but the base room has several separate causal effects and a dual-target boss condition.
The first-pass packet says the optional hint remained closed.

control_friction.rationale: The source and screen provide separate key groups, but the authorized current-native route artifacts do not test a two-human shared keyboard for ghosting or simultaneous-key reliability. Control friction remains unknown.

evidence.claim: The idle packet records no key presses and says controls were not demonstrated.
The replay uses recorded inputs in a native engine, not two-human keyboard testing.

confidence_reason: Current authored source and multiple ordinary-input routes support the pad chain, both-exit condition, and sampled corrections. They establish scripted feasibility only, not human discovery, control comfort, the cost of an unsupported fall, or the frequency of mistakes. During the source phase, a broad validator lookup incidentally printed snippets from an excluded prior second-pass record; I did not use those snippets. These ratings were derived from the current mechanics, cues, route evidence, rubric, and my locked first pass; I do not claim numerical independence from historical judgments.

confirmed: The screenshot's STOP/STEADY/RESCUE labels and separate exits correctly suggested a multi-role route; source confirms distinct Isp and Pac pad ownership and both-exit completion.
The first pass treated bubble handling as a possible test rather than a required route; current source replays confirm a both-exit completion can avoid bubble effects.
missed_mechanics: Source reveals an exact dependency chain from Isp STOP to Pac STEADY to Isp RESCUE, with each stage restoring access or support for the other hero.
Gem adds owner-specific TARGET pads that must be occupied at once before the matching exits count; this was not established by the idle screenshots.
The bubble is a projectile with temporary Isp FLOAT/Pac STICKY effects and a descending Pac top-bounce case; STEADY/RESCUE interrupt it.
incorrect_inferences: No explicit first-pass mechanic claim was contradicted. Possible bubble-route and platform interpretations were left as hypotheses or unknowns, so source refined them rather than reversing a stated fact.
changed_judgments: Reasoning rises from 2 to 3 because source establishes several dependent pad/gate/platform changes followed by a simultaneous boss-target condition, beyond the single visible bubble inference.
Cooperation rises from 2 to 4 because Isp and Pac repeatedly enable each other's crossings and then must occupy separate targets together; distinct roles and repeated mutual dependency are mandatory.
Timing changes from unknown to 1 because the ferry has a repeatable motion/power cycle, while STEADY and RESCUE override its power state during the important crossing; no narrow window is authored.

Hazards changes from unknown to 2 because source places lethal slime and Gem's core under/near the ferry/bridge route, although safe support pads and four no-death samples show a viable supported approach.

Recovery cost changes from unknown to 2 because one current-input case recovers from Pac's early STEADY release and another waits for a later bubble boost; neither tests a lethal fall, which remains unresolved.
Execution stays 2: the moving ferry and stabilized bridge add movement and pad-placement work, but the source route and sampled outcomes do not support sustained precision demand.

Novelty and solution clarity stay at 2: the pad and bridge ideas have earlier introductions, while the simultaneous boss targets are a new combination; visible labels help, but the dependency order is not shown in the idle scene.
unresolved: No human pair attempted either route, so player success, time, enjoyment, frustration, and two-person keyboard comfort are unmeasured.
No allowed route tests a lethal fall or restart after both supports are lost; the high-cost recovery case is unknown.
The two optional collectibles are defined, but the replay summaries do not report whether they were collected or how much detour a novice would take.
The native replay verifies sampled input sequences at current source, not that a first-time pair will infer the pad order from the base cues.

single_operator_note: One person controlling both heroes would need to coordinate W/A/D and arrow-key movement while maintaining a pad hold, then coordinate both TARGET pads. That adds simultaneous-input and attention demand beyond the two-human scores; no keyboard ghosting or single-operator performance was measured.
